discussion_comments.comment_body:
I was assuming that the throw would include the line number so easy enough to track down, but I do like adding the subcommand name. Easier to jump into fixing.

Adding the parent command name is lower value and makes the code harder to read.
```suggestion
      throw new Error(`passThroughOptions cannot be used for '${command._name}' without turning on enablePositionalOptions for parent command(s)`);
```

I agree the parent command name is not important here.

I have actually been working on a proof of concept PR introducing support for multiple parent commands. But before it is added, I wonder what exactly is the purpose of the `(s)` part at the end of the error message?

For safety, positional options should be turned on all the way up the tree. In general I expect it will be turned on at the root, and that intermediate levels won't have options, so unlikely to have a practical effect, and not attempting to robustly enforce. But I thought it was worth adding the `(s)` to hint at the multiple levels.

An alternative to throwing would be to log a warning and carry on, so preserving existing behaviour but encouraging more careful coding by author. This does increase risk authors miss the change in behaviour as unit tests still likely to pass, but does not hard-break end users. Thoughts?

(On that note, some authors have asked why they need to call `.parseAsync()` when `.parse()` seems to work fine for them.)
I like the idea, see [385fe48](https://github.com/tj/commander.js/pull/1915/commits/385fe48b00ce0bfdab8702bf83e899893ef65b5f).

discussion_comments.comment_body: Still adding argDetails to `_args` here.
can you explain me what is the case were argDetails is undefined? I see it's something with the arg name, in which case an argument doesn't have a name?

In the original `_parseExpectedArgs`, if an argument is not in the expected format then the argument is silently ignored because the name does not get set. For example: `{oops}` or `foo` or `<...>`. 

In the refactored code that leads to undefined being returned from `parseArg`.

So I wonder what we should do in that case if we use the Argument class...
It's a bit weird that the initialization of the class fails silently. I would say that it's better to throw an error if the argument is invalid, but it's a breaking change, so i think we should do it later and I'll try to work around it for now.
Ok, after thinking about it again I realized that it's not a breaking change because we can do it only for the new synax. So what do you say? Do you think we should throw on bad argument?
Yes. Throw on bad programmer input is a direction we are slowly moving.

@shadowspawn I have added a throw inside the class, but I can't solve this comment because we don't want to introduce a breaking change so I still need to use argDetails instead of the Argument class here.
when we deprecate `arguments` prop we could remove all usage of argDetails.
I do not think need to error? My earlier comment about wondering what use case there was for both was about understanding existing patterns rather than about preventing both.

Preventing both does make it easier though. We can’t really differentiate between the two. If someone has both and it’s not an error either they both get called which seems unexpected, or only one gets called and it won’t be immediately obvious which. 

I really do think it’d be good to error for this case.

If someone has both then calling them both is backwards compatible, so that is my preferred behaviour.

I don't see why people would want to define both, but I don't see a significant benefit in blocking it. I don't recall seeing reported issues about people wanting different behaviours when defining both — either wanting just one called,  or being confused by calling both.

I do empathise with wanting to reduce the number of possible scenarios since we had trouble reasoning about it, but not at the cost of breaking code patterns we didn't think of.
I updated this as suggested

same sub command was registered twice.
Previously it work because events was overridden.
But inside `commands` array it was two instances with same name.
This lead to problem with help messages and should be handled in separate commit.
IMHO, exception should be thrown then duplicated commands registered.
